name: creative-writing
description: Iterative fiction writing evaluated for voice, sensory precision, and narrative control.

scenarios.name: The Last Ferry Opening
scenarios.description: Draft and refine an opening that establishes a distinctive voice, place, and narrative question.
scenarios.prompt: Write the opening 500–700 words of a literary mystery. On the final ferry to a storm-isolated island, a burned-out marine biologist recognizes a suitcase that belonged to her brother, who disappeared twelve years ago. Establish a distinctive first-person voice, make the ferry and weather tangible, and end on a discovery that forces her to act. Do not explain the brother's disappearance yet.
scenarios.participantPersona: a discerning developmental editor who responds to the draft and requests one concrete, high-leverage revision each round

criteria.name: voice
criteria.description: The narrator has a specific, consistent perspective with language that feels authored rather than generic.

criteria.name: imagery
criteria.description: Sensory details make the ferry, storm, and emotional tension vivid without overcrowding the prose.

criteria.name: coherence
criteria.description: Character motivation, pacing, clues, and revisions form a clear opening arc with a compelling final turn.

scenarios.name: A Refillable Cleaning Kit Launch
scenarios.description: Write and revise a concise launch email that sells a practical refill routine without unsupported claims.
scenarios.prompt: Write a launch email for our refillable household cleaning-spray starter kit. It costs $28 and contains one empty 500 mL glass spray bottle and three individually wrapped concentrate tablets. Each tablet makes 500 mL of cleaner when dissolved in tap water, so the kit makes three bottles of cleaner in total. Future refill packs contain three tablets and cost $9; the glass bottle is reused. The cleaner is intended for sealed counters and glazed tile, not natural stone or unfinished wood. Our audience is apartment renters who dislike storing bulky spare bottles but are skeptical of lofty environmental promises. Our voice is warm, practical, and lightly witty. Give them a concrete reason to try it and one clear call to action to shop the kit. The hard length limit is under 150 words for the entire deliverable, including the subject line, preview text, body, and call to action. Do not add commentary outside the email. Use only the supplied facts: we have no certifications, comparative cleaning tests, health claims, shipping offer, launch discount, or quantified waste savings to cite. Keep the price and what is included clear through revisions.
scenarios.participantPersona: a demanding marketing lead reviewing an email for skeptical apartment renters; give one specific revision request per round, focusing first on replacing a generic claim with a concrete small-space benefit and then on making the purchase action clearer; enforce the under-150-word total and preserve the supplied prices, contents, and surface limits; never request an unsupported claim or a new offer

criteria.name: clarity
criteria.description: Keeps the complete email under 150 words with a subject, preview, body, and clear action; accurately conveys the $28 kit, empty reusable bottle, three tablets, and any refill or surface details used.

criteria.name: persuasion
criteria.description: Connects the refill routine to a concrete renter benefit and a credible reason to buy, without invented savings, certifications, performance claims, or urgency.

criteria.name: brand_voice
criteria.description: Sounds warm, practical, and lightly witty rather than preachy or generic; incorporates revision notes while retaining factual accuracy and a coherent email.

scenarios.name: Owning a Sale Weekend Outage
scenarios.description: Write a public apology that takes responsibility and explains the exact recovery offer.
scenarios.prompt: Write a public social post for our small stationery shop after its website was unavailable for three days during a sale. The outage ran from Friday at 9 a.m. to Monday at 9 a.m., all Eastern Time. A checkout update caused the failure; we do not have evidence of a security incident and should not speculate about one. The site is now working, but we cannot promise it will never fail again. Here is the actual compensation: the original 20% sitewide discount has been restored automatically from Monday at 9 a.m. through Thursday at 9 a.m. Eastern Time, giving shoppers a fresh 72 hours. No code is needed. It applies to merchandise, excludes shipping and gift cards, and cannot be combined with other discounts. We are not offering extra credits or free shipping. Some shoppers reported pending card authorizations without an order confirmation; support can check these through the site's Contact page, but we have not confirmed which became charges and cannot promise a refund date in this post. Write in a plain, accountable voice, own the disruption without blaming a supplier, explain the offer and its limits clearly, and give those with payment concerns a private next step. Do not ask people to post order or payment details publicly.
scenarios.participantPersona: a demanding communications editor who wants an apology that a disappointed shopper would believe; request one concrete revision at a time, first challenging any defensive or evasive wording and then checking the offer deadline and payment-help instructions; retain all offer limits and known facts, and reject invented compensation, outage explanations, or guarantees

criteria.name: accountability
criteria.description: Directly acknowledges the three-day disruption during the sale, takes responsibility for the checkout update, and avoids excuses, blame shifting, or guarantees against future failure.

criteria.name: offer_clarity
criteria.description: Accurately communicates the restored automatic 20% discount, fresh 72-hour window and Eastern Time deadline, shipping and gift-card exclusions, and no stacking without inventing extra compensation.

criteria.name: trust_and_tone
criteria.description: Uses a human, restrained public voice and improves it through revision; directs payment concerns to private support without confusing pending authorizations with confirmed charges or promising refunds.

scenarios.name: A Skillet Page Worth Reading
scenarios.description: Turn a flat specification list into useful sales copy while preserving every product fact and care limit.
scenarios.prompt: Rewrite this bland description into a product page for home cooks buying their first cast-iron skillet: 'Cast-iron skillet. Price $48. Cooking surface diameter 10 inches; rim diameter 12 inches. Weight 6 pounds. One long handle and one helper handle, both cast iron. Two pour spouts. Pre-seasoned with vegetable oil. Suitable for gas, electric, ceramic, and induction stovetops. Oven-safe to 500 F. Hand-wash, dry immediately, and lightly oil after use. Not dishwasher-safe. Handles get hot; use oven mitts. Lid not included.' Keep every factual specification, dimension distinction, compatibility statement, care instruction, and limitation. Build a page with a headline, a short opening, scannable benefits and specifications, care guidance, and a clear buying action. The voice should be confident and welcoming to beginners who worry that cast iron is too much work. Translate facts into useful cooking or handling benefits without claiming it is nonstick, maintenance-free, lightweight, dishwasher-safe, or backed by an unstated warranty. Do not invent country of origin, reviews, certifications, accessories, discounts, or scarcity. Supply finished page copy rather than advice about writing it.
scenarios.participantPersona: a demanding ecommerce editor serving first-time cast-iron buyers; give one actionable revision note per round, first asking for a more concrete beginner benefit and then clearer care or handling guidance; check that the $48 price and every supplied specification remain, especially the 10-inch cooking surface versus 12-inch rim, six-pound weight, hot handles, and missing lid; do not introduce new product facts

criteria.name: factual_fidelity
criteria.description: Preserves every supplied specification and limitation across revisions, including price, both diameters, weight, handles, spouts, seasoning, stovetops, oven limit, care, hot-handle warning, and lid exclusion.

criteria.name: useful_persuasion
criteria.description: Turns relevant features into concrete benefits for a beginner and provides a clear buying action without unsupported performance, ease-of-care, accessory, warranty, or promotional claims.

criteria.name: readability_and_voice
criteria.description: Produces a scannable, coherent product page with a confident, welcoming voice; makes care and handling easy to understand and incorporates editorial notes without losing required facts.
